title: Institutional and financial capital has taken large, but not uniformly controlling, ownership positions across the major diversified berry-genetics groups reviewed
rationale: Three of the largest diversified berry genetics/production groups in this dataset changed ownership structure within roughly a 15-month window (December 2022 - February 2024), and in two of the three cases the incoming owner is a financial or institutional investor rather than an operating berry company. In December 2022, PSP Investments (a Canadian public-sector pension investment manager) together with SJF Investment acquired 49.56% of Hortifrut S.A. In February 2024, a consortium of Paine Schwartz Partners (a specialist food-and-agribusiness private equity firm), Driscoll's, Inc. (an operating berry company) and British Columbia Investment Management Corporation (a Canadian public pension fund manager) took control of Costa Group Holdings at A$3.20/share, which led to Costa's delisting from the ASX days later. Separately, Cinven (a private equity firm) exited its stake in Planasa by selling to EW Group, a German family-owned genetics group -- an ownership transition between two non-operating financial/family owners rather than into operating hands. Taken together, these three transactions suggest berry genetics/production assets are increasingly attractive to institutional and specialist-PE capital, not only to breeding companies themselves. This should be read as a directional pattern across a small number of large, visible transactions (n=3), not a market-wide census -- the dataset does not establish base rates for ownership change in this sector, so 'increasingly attractive' describes the direction suggested by these cases, not a measured trend. It should also not be read as uniform loss of founder/family control: Hortifrut's own 2023 integrated annual report still records the Moller, Quevedo, Del Rio and Elberg families as 'the controlling group' even after the PSP/SJF transaction, since 49.56% is a very large minority stake, not majority control -- see counterevidence. The Costa consortium is also not purely financial: Driscoll's is an operating berry company with its own genetics and brand interests, so 'financial capital' is directionally but not entirely accurate there either.
why_it_matters: Ownership links can change disclosure, licensing posture and whether nominal competitors remain economically independent.
would_change_our_view: Transaction reversals, disclosed passive-only holdings, or evidence that licensing and disclosure remain unchanged.
